tasks.title: Laravel security fix in this repo (project root): mass-assignment hardening of the legacy h-r-leave module. Files: app/Http/Controllers/HumanResources/HRLeaveController.php, app/Http/Requests/HumanResources/StoreHRLeaveRequest.php, app/Http/Requests/HumanResources/UpdateHRLeaveRequest.php, app/Models/HumanResources/HRLeave.php. Context: the base model app/Models/Model.php sets protected $guarded = [] (everything mass-assignable), the store() method does HRLeave::create($request->except('_token')) and $result->hasManyRelationship()->createMany($request->arrays), and update() does $hRLeave->update($request->except('_token', '_method')). Both Form Requests are make:module scaffolds that validate only a placeholder 'ColumnName' => ['required'] rule. Fix: (1) in StoreHRLeaveRequest, replace the placeholder rules with real validation for the fields the legacy form posts (check resources/views/h-r-leave/_form.blade.php and create.blade.php for the actual field names — date_time_start, date_time_end, reason, leave_type_id, staff_id, and the nested 'arrays' structure used by createMany; use 'required'/'sometimes'/'integer'/'date'/'string' rules with attributes() and messages() mirroring the working app/Http/Requests/HumanResources/Leave/HRLeaveRequestStore.php as a reference); (2) fix UpdateHRLeaveRequest: set authorize() to true and give it real rules for the same fields; (3) in HRLeaveController.store(), replace $request->except('_token') with $request->validated() (and pass only the validated 'arrays' key to createMany — guard with isset($request->validated()['arrays'])); (4) in HRLeaveController.update(), replace $request->except('_token', '_method') with $request->validated(); (5) add an explicit protected $fillable = [...] array to the HRLeave model listing every column from the table (inspect the migration database/migrations/*create_hr_leaves_table* or the SQL dump for the columns) so the guarded=[] base can no longer mass-assign arbitrary request keys. Do NOT change the new module app/Http/Controllers/HumanResources/Leave/HRLeaveController.php or HRLeaveRequestStore.php — they are already safe. Then run php -l on every changed file and php artisan test to confirm nothing broke.

Laravel security fix in this repo (project root): eliminate the remaining $request->except('_token') mass-assignment call sites in the HRDept controllers. Files to fix: app/Http/Controllers/HumanResources/HRDept/AnnualLeaveController.php (line ~87: $annualleave->update($request->except(['_method', '_token']))), app/Http/Controllers/HumanResources/HRDept/AppraisalSettingController.php (line ~50: $appraisalsetting->update($request->except(['_token', 'id']))), app/Http/Controllers/HumanResources/HRDept/HolidayCalendarController.php (store ~68: HRHolidayCalendar::create($request->except(['_token'])) and update ~95: ->update($request->except(['_token', '_method']))), app/Http/Controllers/HumanResources/HRDept/MCLeaveController.php (update ~86), app/Http/Controllers/HumanResources/HRDept/MaternityLeaveController.php (update ~86). Context: these controllers type-hint the base Illuminate\Http\Request (no Form Request), and the models HRLeaveAnnual, HRAppraisalSetting, HRHolidayCalendar, HRLeaveMC, HRLeaveMaternity inherit $guarded = [] from app/Models/Model.php, so every posted key is mass-assigned with zero validation. Fix: for EACH of the five controllers, (1) determine the actual form field names from the matching blade view (resources/views/humanresources/hrdept/<module>/... _form.blade.php / create.blade.php / edit.blade.php) and the target model's table columns (inspect the migration or SQL dump); (2) replace the $request->except(...) call with $request->only([...]) passing an explicit whitelist of exactly those field names (do NOT create new Form Request classes — keep the change surgical and self-contained); (3) add an explicit protected $fillable = [...] to each of the five models (HRLeaveAnnual, HRAppraisalSetting, HRHolidayCalendar, HRLeaveMC, HRLeaveMaternity) listing their table columns, so the guarded=[] base cannot mass-assign arbitrary keys. Preserve all existing behavior: same fields stored, same values, same validation errors path (none existed). Then run php -l on every changed file and php artisan test to confirm nothing broke (the suite currently has 31 passing tests).

Write a unit test for the mass-assignment hardening in this repo (project root) and run the test suite. Create tests/Unit/MassAssignmentGuardTest.php: a plain PHPUnit test (no database) with two source-level guards: (1) read app/Http/Controllers/HumanResources/HRLeaveController.php and app/Http/Controllers/HumanResources/HRDept/{AnnualLeaveController,AppraisalSettingController,HolidayCalendarController,MCLeaveController,MaternityLeaveController}.php as strings and assert none of them contains the patterns $request->except('_token') or $request->except(['_token', '_method']) or $request->except(['_method', '_token']) or $request->except(['_token', 'id']) (the request input must be whitelisted via ->only([...]) or ->validated() before create/update); (2) read app/Models/Model.php and assert it still declares protected $guarded = [] (documenting that per-model $fillable is the project's chosen defense), and read the six models app/Models/HumanResources/{HRLeave,HRLeaveAnnual,HRAppraisalSetting,HRHolidayCalendar,HRLeaveMC,HRLeaveMaternity}.php asserting each declares a non-empty protected $fillable array. Also assert app/Http/Requests/HumanResources/StoreHRLeaveRequest.php and UpdateHRLeaveRequest.php contain real rules (e.g. the string 'date_time_start' appears in the rules array and 'ColumnName' does not). Run php artisan test — the suite must stay green (currently 31 passing tests / 72 assertions) — and report the run result with the test report contract.
